summary: Reviewed src/config/config.ts (lines 253–262) and src/tests/config.test.ts (lines 434–446). The change replaces two error messages in parseGitCredentials() that previously interpolated the raw hostname (${host}) with a positional-index format (entry #${index + 1} (legacy format)). 0 Critical, 0 High findings. 1 Info observation (noted below). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A02/A09 — Positive security change. The pre-existing code interpolated ${host} (a user-supplied hostname read from config.json) into thrown Error messages. Those messages could surface in server logs or monitoring systems, potentially leaking internal/private infrastructure hostnames. The fix replaces host interpolation with a positional index (index + 1, integer arithmetic) and typeof token (a fixed JS type literal — always one of 'number', 'boolean', 'object', etc.). Neither carries sensitive data. This is a net-positive reduction in information disclosure risk.

A03 — Injection not applicable. The error string is composed exclusively of: (a) a static literal prefix, (b) integer arithmetic on a loop counter (index + 1), (c) typeof token — a language keyword result, not user-controlled input. No user-supplied string is interpolated. No injection surface exists in these two error paths.

Info — Full OWASP Top 10 sweep on modified scope: A01 (access control) — not applicable (config parsing, no access decisions made in these lines). A04 (insecure design) — the new positional format still provides actionable diagnostic context without sensitive data leakage; design is sound. A05 (misconfiguration) — no stack trace or internal path exposed. A06 (components) — no new dependencies introduced. A07 (auth failures) — not applicable to config-parsing layer. A08 (integrity) — no deserialization or update mechanism touched. A10 (SSRF) — no URL fetching involved. All categories clear.

The two error-throw branches are structurally identical to their surroundings and follow the established throw-on-invalid-value pattern used throughout parseGitCredentials().

Best Practices: PASS — the fix avoids interpolating user-supplied external data (the hostname) into error strings, aligning with the project convention observed in git-cli.ts and the new-format array validation paths. DRY is respected: the legacy-format branch is already isolated; no duplication introduced. SOLID not directly applicable at this granularity.
Performance: PASS — no performance implications. The change is two string literal modifications inside a validation loop that runs once at startup.

Future Context: PASS — the legacy-format branch exists purely for backward-compatibility migration. The positional-index format is strictly more maintainable than host-interpolated messages: it remains valid even if the host value changes between config edits, and it avoids accidental information leakage in future log shipping scenarios. No technical debt introduced.
